messages:
june: Heads-up — we'll run the canary region swap tomorrow 09:00 UTC. Planning a soft-swap: 10% traffic probe for 15m, then 50% for 10m if metrics look good. Quick sanity check on residency heuristics + lease behavior?

omar: Two quick flags: 1) KV ownership transitions — any write routed to new region must either prewarm or fall back to primary; otherwise latency spikes. 2) In-flight requests: need a clear drain/forwarding window so clients don’t see partial failures.

kevin: Agreed on both. My proposal:
- probe_window: 900s (15m) for initial health + read-only consistency checks
- lease_ttl: 30s with randomized jitter to avoid thundering herd
- failure_threshold: 3 consecutive probe fails -> abort
Example routing config (pseudo):
```json
{"probe_window_s":900, "lease_ttl_s":30, "failure_threshold":3, "post_swap_drain_s":45}
```

amina: Residency/GDPR note: writes for tenants with residency=EU must never land in non-EU write paths. Plan: edge token includes residency claim, router enforces write pinning. Reads can be proxied from another region but must be sanitized and logged. We should also add an explicit header when a swap is allowed: `X-Resident-Write-Allowed: true` so downstream can short-circuit.

marta: How does that work for Dedicated customers with on-prem private deployments? We can’t assume the same global routing fabric.

kevin: For Dedicated/Private we rely on control-plane flags pushed to their local proxy. Each proxy keeps the same lease semantics locally. In practice: control-plane triggers prewarm snapshot push -> proxy switches route predicate when local health probes pass. If snapshot push fails, abort and roll back.

omar: Also: KV cache warming strategy — snapshot vs tailing replication. Snapshot is faster to prewarm cold keys; tailing keeps consistent but is heavier. For this canary I vote snapshot prewarm of hot prefixes (top-1k keys by QPS).

june: Good call. We'll do hot-prefix snapshot prewarm + tailing for the rest. Prewarm numbers: 1k keys per canary shard, aim to finish within probe_window.

kevin: Edge-case: primary unhealthy longer than grace window. We should have a forced-eviction flow:
1) escalate to on-call (automated)
2) allow writes with residency-warning header and audit log
3) fallback TTL shortens to 10s and we enable synchronous cross-region replicate to satisfy compliance when possible
That keeps apps alive but surfaces risk.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled route-change job created for 2026-03-21T09:00Z (canary) by june. Runbook link: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/region-swap> :spiral_note_pad:

marta: One more ask for runbook: add a step to validate audit logs contain `resident_claim` for every write that left the primary region. Also include a rollback checklist with exact CLI commands.

june: Will update runbook before EOD. Final checklist items I'll add: prewarm snapshot status, probe pass metrics (p99 latency, error-rate), audit log residency check, and automated rollback trigger if failure_threshold hit. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
